question.leadin: Ozan Kilinc ("KILL-inch") was jailed by a court in this country for publishing articles sympathetic to a banned party.
question.text: Name this country, where insulting the country or the government is illegal under Article 301.
question.clue: This country's penal code includes a controversial Article 301 that has been used to crack down on dissidents who have discussed the Armenian Genocide orchestrated by this country.

swap.leadin: The Golden Horn cuts into this city and was once spanned by a large chain to prevent enemy ships from getting in.
swap.text: Name this Turkish city that was previously named Byzantium and Constantinople.
swap.clue: Cannons designed by the Hungarian engineer Orban were used to breach this city's Theodosian Walls.

question.text: In the 1910s and 20s, the Young Turks perpetrated a genocide on this ethnic group, in which the Ottoman Empire forced this group from their homeland. The modern Turkish government refuses to identify the event as a genocide.
question.answerHtml: Armenians (accept Armenian genocide or Armenian Holocaust, but do not prompt on Holocaust)
question.clue: Thanks to Gregory the Illuminator, these people had the world's first official Christian state starting in 301.

swap.leadin: A huge amount of impressive building projects were designed by this ruler's architect, Sinan.
swap.text: Name this son of Selim the Grim, who won the Battle of Mohacs [Moe-HOTCH] but was less successful in conquering Malta and also led an unsuccessful siege of Vienna.
swap.answerHtml: Suleiman the Magnificent [or Suleiman the Lawgiver or Suleiman I; prompt on “Suleiman”]
swap.clue: This man's forces defeated the Knights Hospitaller during the 1522 Siege of Rhodes, but Spanish intervention prevented a second victory during the Great Siege of Malta.

question.leadin: Many of those who orchestrated this event were assassinated during Operation Nemesis.
question.text: Identify this event in which over a million people of a certain Caucasian nationality were forcibly resettled and killed, perpetrated by the Ottoman Empire during World War I.
question.answerHtml: Armenian Genocide (accept equivalents like Armenian Massacre; prompt on “Great Crime” or “Medz Yeghern”)
question.clue: To raise money for this event's victims, Cleveland Dodge founded the ACASR at the urging of Henry Morgenthau Sr. While reporting for the Agos, Hrant Dink was murdered in 2007 for discussing this event and violating one country's Article 301.

swap.text: The Fatih Mosque and Tiled Kiosk were built during the reign of this Ottoman sultan, who took Constantinople in May 1453 to earn the epithet "Conqueror."
swap.clue: This ruler established a millet led by Gennadius II, who received authority over all Orthodox Christians in his empire.

question.text: The English use of stakes at Agincourt may have been inspired by this battle, where the Ottomans routed a crusader army.
question.clue: Stefan Lazarevich's Serbs took part in this battle as vassals of the winning side.

swap.leadin: Answer some questions about reactions to the Ottoman invasions of the Balkans.
swap.text: Following the assassination of Sultan Murad I during the Battle of Kosovo, this man known as "the Thunderbolt" became sultan and went on to defeat the Crusade of Nicopolis in Bulgaria.
swap.clue: This man's reign was followed by a twelve year power struggle known as the Interregnum before the confirmation of Mehmet I as sultan.

question.leadin: Identify these groups of Muslim soldiers.
question.text: Prior to the 1826 Auspicious Incident, this group of Ottoman Empire soldiers was staffed by youths of Christian families who were recruited in the devishirme.
question.clue: When these people were eliminated, the closely-associated sect of Bektashi Sufism was banned.

swap.text: This period of Ottoman reform began with the 1839 "Noble Edict of the Rose Chamber." The reforms of this period, whose name means "reorganization," eliminated millet courts.

question.text: After the Turkish nationalists rallied to defeat the Greeks, Armenians, and French, this new treaty replaced, and returned all of the concessions of, Sevres.
question.clue: An earlier treaty signed at the same location was also called the Treaty of Ouchy, and ended the Italo-Turkish War in 1912.

swap.text: This son of the Kayi tribe leader Ertugrul founded the Ottoman Dynasty after throwing off the yoke of the Seljuks.
swap.answerHtml: Osman I [or Osman Gazi; or Osman Bey; or Othman I El-Gazi; or Osman Sayed II]
swap.clue: This figure's father Ertugrul was a member of the Kayi tribe, and along with troops known as the Ghazi warriors, this man was victorious over George Mouzalon and his Byzantine forces at the Battle of Bapheus.

question.leadin: The Turkish television series Magnificent Century, a historic drama that caused controversy over its portrayal of Ottoman rulers, gets its name from this ruler's epithet "the Magnificent."
question.text: Name this Ottoman ruler, often called "The Lawgiver", who reigned between 1520 and 1566.
question.answerHtml: Suleiman I [or Suleiman the Magnificent; or Suleiman the Lawgiver; or Süleyman-ı Evvel; or Ḳānūnī Sulṭān Süleymān]
question.clue: This ruler expelled the Knights Hospitalers from Rhodes after conquering Belgrade, although the same group would defeat him at Malta later on.

swap.text: In 1845, a holder of this title wrote the treatise "Benefits to Children" describing vaccine efforts for a cowpox outbreak. Holders of this Ottoman title like Enver and Cemal ["jamal"] led a "Young Turk Triumvirate" shadow government until the empire's collapse post-WWI.
swap.clue: The genocide was carried out by the Committee of Union and Progress under three de facto leaders with this title. Talaat and Ahmed Cemal ("keh-mal"), who both had this title, were assassinated for their role in the genocide during Operation Nemesis.

question.text: Soon after the Auspicious Incident, the Ottoman army was modernized during this wider initiative. The introduction of paper money and post offices, as well as units called vilayets, were among the changes introduced during this initiative.
question.clue: This period of reform in the Ottoman Empire begun by the Rescript of the Rose Chamber. This period included the abolition of the millet system and the elimination of tax farming.

swap.text: In this 1826 event, Sultan Mahmud II had most of the elite Janissaries killed after they revolted at the institution of westernized troops.
swap.clue: This massacre of soldiers perpetrated by Mahmud II.

question.leadin: Name these types of troops in the Ottoman Empire.
question.text: These irregular troops, named for the beggars of Istanbul, were notorious for their brutality. Following their lack of discipline during the Crimean War and the Russo-Turkish War of 1877, they were disbanded.
question.clue: This irregular Ottoman troops whose Turkish name means "disorderly heads" in reference to their tendency to loot. Gladstone's Midlothian campaign denounced these units' involvement in the "Bulgarian horrors."

swap.leadin: Answer the following about men who ruled Libya.
swap.text: This dynasty previously ruled Libya from 1711 to 1835 after seizing power from the Ottoman bey and setting up a semi-autonomous state. This dynasty included Yusuf, who initiated the first Barbary War by deposing his brother Hamet and demanding tribute from Thomas Jefferson.

question.text: As with the various denominations of Christians in the empire, this system granted the Ottoman Jewish community much autonomy over their internal affairs.
question.clue: This system, which allowed religious minorities to live independently of Islamic law, was abolished by the Tanzimat reforms in an attempt to reduce nationalist tendencies.

swap.leadin: Name these groups of Europeans within the Ottoman Empire.
swap.text: The Cantacuino and Ypsilanti families were part of this class of leading residents of Constantinople's Greek quarter. They were the namesake of the eighteenth century in Romanian history because they were appointed as hospodars there, and they controlled the selection of the Orthodox patriarch.
swap.clue: In the 18th century, this class of Greek merchant families dominated Ottoman government positions such as Grand Dragoman of the Fleet and Hospodar of Moldavia. They were named after a Greek neighborhood in Istanbul.
